newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan president sacks three ministers, one quits.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan president sacks three ministers, one quits.

text.p: Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu has fired three cabinet ministers and demoted his finance minister while the powerful Hutu interior minister has resigned, a presidential aide said on Saturday.
Joseph Bideri told Reuters by telephone from the capital Kigali that Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Colonel Alexis Kanyarengwe resigned late on Friday.

Kanyarengwe, a Hutu, is also chairman of the ruling Rwanda Patriotic Front and led the Tutsi-dominated RPF into victory in 1994 after many years in exile that began when he fell out with the administration of late Hutu strongman Juvenal Habyarimana.

The Hutus fled in 1994 during civil war in fear of reprisals for the three-month mass slaughter of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs that followed Habyarimana's death when his plane was shot down.
The RPF first invaded the tiny Central African nation in 1990 from Uganda where commanders such as military supremo and Vice-President Major-General Paul Kagame served in the army.
Bideri said Kanyarengwe resigned of his own accord: "It was his own decision because he wants to concentrate on his other jobs."

But political analysts expressed surprise at the departure of the ambitious Kanyarengwe. "It is a surprise move because in essence it takes a lot of clout from him," said an exiled influential member of Rwanda's Hutu community.
Finance Minister Marc Rugenera was demoted to the handicraft, mining and tourism post. Little-known Jean Birara was appointed finance minister with economist Donat Kaberuka as his minister of state.
Kaberuka has worked at the Abidjan-based Inter-African Coffee Organisation as chief economist for the last 10 years.
Bideri cautioned against reading too much into the changes, saying the "whole exercise is a normal one. Kanyarengwe wants to concentrate on other jobs he occupies."

Bideri said Bizimungu, also a Hutu, had retained Kagame as vice-president and defence minister. Kagame is also chairman of the military high command, which makes him the most powerful politician in Rwanda.
Prime Minister Pierre Celestin Rwigema and Foreign Affairs Minister Anastase Gasana kept their jobs.
Bideri said Transport and Telecommunications Minister Charles Muligande, Social Affairs Minister Pie Mugabo and Industry and Commerce Minister Prosper Higiro had been fired.

The new interior minister is Sheikh Abdulkarim Harelimana, previously public service minister, while Joseph Nsengimana was moved from higher education to public service. Charles Ntakirutinka was named minister of communications and Bonaventure Niyibizi commerce minister.
Health Minister Joseph Karemera was moved to the education post while Vincent Biruta was named health minister and Jean Nayinzira was appointed information minister.
The rehabilitation ministry has been abolished and its minister Patrick Mazimhaka was named minister in the presidency.
